label: second copy step (output orig[1]) in long sequences, L>=8
explanation: Fires only at step L+1, the first copy step after <DEL> (input = orig[0], output = orig[1]). It never fires in the original phase, at the delimiter, or at any other copy position. It needs long sequences: there are no activations for L<=5, the rate is 0.5% at L=6 recall step... rising to about 20% at L=8 and 35% at L=9, and L=9 carries 63% of the activation mass. The predicate recall_idx==1 & L>=8 covers 92% of the mass but has low precision (0.27). Within that slot, token content shapes firing and magnitude in a distributed way: rates are higher when orig[1] or orig[2] is one of p/o/t/z/j/3/2, when orig[0] is z/r/m/n, and when there are more digits. The strongest examples (for example z p ..., r z t ..., 2 t t ...) often have t at position 2. No single token rule captures this; adding a token-set clause raises F1 only to 0.52.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the second original token (most: p, o, z, t, j, 2; least: y, d, l, v) and the next token to output (most: t, 3, p, o, j, z; least: -, v, w, n); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=10, L=8 & t=9.
